response.markdown_report:
Select **endpoint-preserving temporal patching**: test whether earlier-context information changes predictions through an intermediate NextItNet state, while keeping the terminal item fixed.

**Insights from the starting point.** First, frequency-matched old substitutions were less disruptive than random substitutions in Movies and CDs; both absolute old-substitution effects remained negative. This supports weaker sensitivity to older context, without establishing harmful history. Second, the current probe patches only the readout position. Restoration there can reflect representation copying, motivating interventions at earlier occupied positions. Third, exact host validation candidates are unavailable to the adapter. Diagnostic ranking changes therefore cannot establish validation improvement.

**Insights from related work.** NextItNet’s causal dilated convolutions provide depth and temporal coordinates for intervention [1]. Dependency paths must nevertheless be audited before selecting a reachable patch position. Patching outcomes depend on corruption and measurement choices [2]. Endpoint-preserving permutations isolate earlier ordering more narrowly than endpoint replacement. Successful patches can exploit atypical computational pathways [3]. Identity controls and hybrid-state distance checks can flag artifacts but cannot certify faithful mechanisms.

These insights define three directions: temporal specificity, intervention reliability, and evaluation scope. Their conceptual map is:

| Axis | Existing probe | Proposed extension | Remaining gap |
|---|---|---|---|
| Input | Endpoint/order perturbations | Endpoint-preserving order contrast | Permutations may be unnatural |
| Mediator | Readout-position states | Earlier occupied state | Unpatched paths remain |
| Evidence | Diagnostic ranks/margins | Paired restoration/disruption | Host validation benefit |

Three atomic ideas follow. Scores are originality/potential/difficulty, each out of ten; higher difficulty means harder implementation.

| Idea | Scores | Positive assessment | Negative assessment |
|---|---|---|---|
| Earlier-position bidirectional patching [1–3] | 5/7/5 | Adds temporal localization; reusable; existing hooks help | Established method; benefit uncertain; reachability audit needed |
| Two-site factorial patching [2,3] | 6/7/7 | Exposes nonadditivity; supports pathway studies; bounded grid | Interactions are scale-dependent; hybrids complicate interpretation; more forwards |
| Candidate-draw stability audit [4] | 3/6/3 | Clarifies measurement sensitivity; broadly useful; simple scoring | Familiar; does not explain mechanisms; catalog scoring costs grow |

At 20% progress, choose the first idea. Prespecify one intermediate block and one earlier occupied position reachable from an edited input and capable of influencing the final readout. Preserve terminal ID, padding, candidates, and original maximum-nonzero readout. Compare clean-to-corrupted restoration and corrupted-to-clean disruption against their respective baselines; report raw margin and rank changes without dividing by small corruption gaps.

Bound execution to 32 uniquely identified training users/category and three permutations, with seed 42. Failed identity, repeatability, shape, or reachability checks invalidate the site. Report user-level paired intervals, coverage, missing reasons, and exploratory status. Keep one checkpoint/category and the pinned macro validation HR@10 selection rule unchanged.

References: [1] NextItNet; [2] Zhang & Nanda, 2024; [3] Makelov et al., 2024; [4] Krichene & Rendle, 2020. Links and limitations appear below.

idea.description: Extend the staged NextItNet diagnostic with endpoint-preserving, earlier-position bidirectional activation patching. Within each category’s single frozen model, perturb earlier ordering and intervene at one prespecified intermediate block-position pair whose audited dependencies connect edited inputs to the original final nonpadding readout.
idea.motivation: The supplied results show category-dependent training sensitivity, not evidence that older history should be removed. The current readout-position patches can copy an already integrated representation. Earlier-position interventions provide a narrower test of how ordering information propagates through the causal convolutional backbone, while preserving endpoint identity and avoiding an additional fitted predictor.
idea.implementation_notes:
Retain DiagnosisProbe(view, device), run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), and diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis). Return metrics and metric_definitions, including counts, exclusions, numerical controls, missing reasons, and formulas. Preserve view.model as the actual trained module and all ModelView interfaces.

Cache at most ten loader batches and retain at most 32 uniquely matched training users per category, one event each. Use local seed 42 and reuse the existing diagnostic candidate IDs across every condition; these candidates are not host validation candidates. Permute only occupied positive-lag positions, preserving terminal ID, padding pattern, sequence width, and item multiset. Count identity permutations and insufficient-history exclusions.

Before observing patch outcomes, select one intermediate block and a deterministic earlier occupied patch position. Audit functional dependencies, including masks, normalization, gates, and residual paths: edited inputs must reach that state and the state must reach the final readout. Convolution span metadata alone is insufficient. If the audit or activation layout cannot be established, return an explicit missing result.

Cache clean and corrupted block outputs. Patch the complete hidden vector at that single earlier position in both directions, using the same model and each recipient’s own baseline. Identity patches must reproduce features and candidate scores within disclosed dtype-aware tolerances. Preserve the original maximum-nonzero readout index, never count-1. Report margin changes, rank changes, diagnostic hit transitions, corruption gaps, and downstream activation-distance flags. Do not label these flags as proof of distributional support or use normalized recovery near zero gaps.

Average permutations within user; bootstrap users only when sufficiently many uniquely identified users remain. Report eligible-only effects and coverage separately. Keep independent donor experiments and factorial extensions deferred to bound runtime. Restore module modes, backend settings, RNG state, and temporary hooks in finally.

No training or deployed inference change is required. Preserve four routes, one independently trained NextItNet checkpoint per category, DATA_DIR=os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], trial-local artifacts, preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, maximum 200 epochs, 200 batches per epoch, and single-GPU execution. This diagnostic does not establish user intent, ownership, compatibility, or host validation gains. Never reconstruct unavailable validation candidates or consume hidden test data.
idea.pseudocode:
def run_full_diagnosis(train_loader):
    saved = save_modes_backends_and_rng(view.model)
    try:
        enter_deterministic_eval(view.model)
        events = cache_and_uniquely_match_training_events(
            train_loader, max_batches=10, max_users=32, seed=42)
        site = prespecify_and_audit_intermediate_temporal_site(events)
        if site is unavailable:
            return metrics_and_definitions_with_missing_reason()
        for event in events:
            last = maximum_nonzero_index(event.sequence)
            candidates = fixed_existing_diagnostic_candidates(event)
            clean = forward_capture(event.sequence, site, last, candidates)
            verify_identity_patch_and_repeatability(clean)
            for corrupted_sequence in three_endpoint_preserving_permutations(event):
                corrupted = forward_capture(corrupted_sequence, site, last, candidates)
                if not audited_reachability_and_controls_pass(event, site):
                    record_exclusion()
                    continue
                restored = forward_with_single_position_patch(
                    corrupted_sequence, site, clean.activation, last, candidates)
                disrupted = forward_with_single_position_patch(
                    event.sequence, site, corrupted.activation, last, candidates)
                record(restored.outcomes - corrupted.outcomes,
                       disrupted.outcomes - clean.outcomes,
                       clean.outcomes - corrupted.outcomes)
        return user_averaged_paired_summaries_with_counts_and_definitions()
    finally:
        remove_hooks_and_restore(saved)

# diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis) includes measured metrics,
# definitions, exclusions, and scope; requests evidence-linked interpretation.

originality.positive: Adds temporal specificity to the supplied readout-only protocol by combining endpoint-preserving corruption with audited earlier-position interventions.
originality.negative: Activation patching and bidirectional controls are established techniques; the novelty is a careful NextItNet adaptation.

future_potential.positive: Could identify reproducible temporal pathways and provide a disciplined basis for later single-model regularization experiments.
future_potential.negative: Intervention-specific localization may not generalize across histories or predict improvements in pinned validation HR@10.

code_difficulty.positive: Reuses existing caches, hooks, candidate scoring, and user-level aggregation without retraining or modifying deployment.
code_difficulty.negative: Reliable functional reachability auditing and activation-layout handling require architecture-specific work beyond adding a hook.

related_work.title: A Simple Convolutional Generative Network for Next Item Recommendation
contributions: Introduces NextItNet’s residual causal dilated convolutional architecture for sequential recommendation.
Provides the architectural basis for interventions indexed by block depth and temporal position.
limitations: Does not establish the proposed activation-patching diagnostic.
The supplied implementation’s complete functional dependencies still require auditing.

related_work.title: Towards Best Practices of Activation Patching in Language Models: Metrics and Methods
contributions: Examines sensitivity of patching conclusions to corruption methods and outcome metrics.
Motivates reporting raw effects with explicit controls and fixed measurement conditions.
limitations: Language-model findings do not validate a recommendation-specific protocol.
Controlled patching effects remain conditional on the chosen interventions.

related_work.title: Interpretability Illusions in the Generalization of Simplified Models
contributions: Demonstrates that apparently successful interpretability interventions can involve pathways disconnected from ordinary computation.
Motivates caution when interpreting hybrid activation states.
limitations: Its subspace-intervention examples do not establish that full-vector temporal patches in NextItNet fail.
Distance and norm controls can flag artifacts but cannot certify faithful mechanisms.

related_work.title: On Sampled Metrics for Item Recommendation
contributions: Shows that sampled recommendation metrics can alter model comparisons.
Supports separating diagnostic candidate results from claims about full-catalog ranking.
limitations: Does not change the task’s mandated pinned evaluator.
Does not establish which diagnostic candidate distribution best captures these users’ needs.
